metaDescription: Snowbird car shipping from New York to Florida: the seasonal calendar, month-by-month prices, booking lead times, fly-and-ship timing, and gated delivery.
h1: Snowbird car shipping from New York to Florida
heroSub: Every fall thousands of New Yorkers send the car south and fly down behind it. Here is the calendar, the price swings, and the logistics that make seasonal car shipping go smoothly both ways.
intro:
Snowbird car shipping is the most predictable thing we do. The same families from Long Island, Westchester, Queens, and upstate ship the same cars to the same Florida condos every autumn and bring them back every spring. The lane is so well traveled that we can tell you within a few days when the trucks fill up and when prices jump.

That works in your favor if you plan around it. Book early in the fall and the New York to Florida snowbird auto transport price is close to the year-round rate. Wait until the week after Christmas and you are competing with everyone in the Northeast for the same spots on the same trucks.

sections.h2: The snowbird car shipping calendar: when the trucks run full
sections.html:
Southbound demand from New York starts building in early October, climbs through November, and peaks from the week after Christmas through the end of January, when retirees who waited for the holidays with family finally head down. It is the hardest window all year to find a truck at a normal price. February stays busy, and by April southbound is quiet.

Northbound runs the mirror image. A trickle starts in March, the real wave hits in April after Easter and Passover, and it tails off by mid-May. In October a driver loads nine cars in the NYC metro for Boca and Naples, delivers, and immediately wants nine more going north so he is not driving an empty trailer up I-95. That empty leg is why prices move the way they do.

sections.h2: Why seasonal car shipping prices swing so much
sections.html:
A hauler earns money only when the trailer is full. In November the southbound trailer is full and the northbound one is empty, so the driver prices southbound cars at full rate and takes a northbound car at a steep discount to cover fuel home. In April it flips. Moving a car against the season picks up that backhaul discount, often $100 to $200.

The baseline open-carrier New York to Florida rate is $650 to $750 for a running mid-size sedan booked about a week out. During the late December and January peak the same move commonly runs $850 to $1,000, and expedited pickup inside that window can push past $1,100. SUVs and pickups add $100 to $250. Enclosed transport adds 30 to 50 percent, worth it to many snowbirds against road salt leaving New York. The pricing guide has the full surcharge list.

sections.h2: When to book snowbird car shipping, and the popular New York to Florida pairs
sections.html:
In October and November, one to two weeks of notice is plenty. From mid-December through January, book two to four weeks ahead. Booking early locks the price and posts your load before drivers build their January runs. Last-minute bookings in peak cost more and land in a wider pickup window. Use the quote tool to see the rate for your dates and how it moves if you shift a week either way.

The pairs we run most: Nassau and Suffolk, including pickups from our Hempstead, Babylon, Islip, and Brookhaven offices, plus Westchester, the Bronx, and Queens, to Boca Raton, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, and West Palm Beach. The Gulf side draws Long Island and upstate customers heading to Naples, Fort Myers, and Sarasota. The Villages and Orlando pull from everywhere, and Buffalo and Albany families lean toward the Gulf coast. Our Buffalo office stages southbound loads through October and November, though upstate pickups run two to three days longer because fewer trucks pass through. The New York to Florida route guide has transit times by region.

sections.h2: Fly-and-ship logistics: timing the car to land after you do
sections.html:
The standard plan is to hand the car to the driver, fly down a day or two later, and take delivery one to three days after landing. The airports line up with the destinations: JFK, LaGuardia, Islip, Albany, and Buffalo to Palm Beach (PBI) for Boca and Delray, Fort Lauderdale (FLL), Fort Myers (RSW) for Naples and the Gulf, Sarasota (SRQ), and Orlando (MCO) for the Villages.

Transit to south Florida is two to four days on the truck, so a car waiting when you land has to be picked up four to five days before your flight. Most people schedule pickup the day before the flight, rent a car at the airport, and take delivery two or three days later. Give us the flight date at booking and we plan pickup around it. Someone has to hand the car over in New York and receive it in Florida; a neighbor or an adult child with the keys works fine.

sections.h2: Gated communities, HOAs, and where the truck can actually stop
sections.html:
Most Florida snowbird destinations are gated. A nine-car hauler is about 75 feet long, and many communities bar commercial trucks from residential streets, so the driver usually meets you at the gatehouse, the clubhouse lot, or a shopping center outside the entrance. That is normal door-to-door service; the driver gets as close as the truck legally can.

Before pickup, ask the community office whether a car hauler may enter, what the gate code or guest-list procedure is, and whether there is a designated delivery area. Some HOAs allow trucks only on weekday mornings or require 24 hours' notice; we put all of it on the dispatch sheet. Co-ops in Queens and many Long Island villages have truck rules too, so a wide lot a few minutes away is usually easier at both ends.

sections.h2: Two cars, round trips, the Auto Train, summer storage, and packing
sections.html:
Two-car households often ship one and drive the other. Booking both cars on one order usually puts them on the same truck and trims the per-car rate. Round-trip booking is worth asking about: if you know in October that the car comes back in April, booking both legs locks the northbound price before the spring rush.

The Amtrak Auto Train is a fair alternative. It runs from Lorton, Virginia to Sanford, Florida, north of Orlando, and you ride with your car. The trade-offs: you drive to Lorton, about 250 miles from the city, then drive from Sanford to the Gulf or Palm Beach coasts. Capacity is limited and sells out in peak weeks. Total cost is often comparable to shipping plus a flight, so it comes down to whether you want two days with the car or a few hours on a plane.

Some snowbirds leave the car in Florida all summer. That saves two shipping legs, but the car sits through hurricane season from June through November with no quick way to move it. Northbound backhaul rates in May are low, which is the argument for bringing it home.

On packing: nothing of value. Carrier cargo insurance covers the vehicle, not its contents. The common tolerance is up to about 100 pounds of personal items in the trunk or below the window line, but policies vary by carrier and a driver can refuse an overloaded car. Golf clubs and a suitcase are usually fine; boxes are not. The shipping checklist covers the rest.

faqs.q: When is the cheapest time to ship a snowbird car from New York to Florida?
faqs.a: October and early November for the southbound trip, when trucks are plentiful and prices sit near the year-round rate of $650 to $750 for a sedan. The late December and January peak adds $200 or more. Northbound, May is cheaper than April. Shipping against the season picks up a backhaul discount.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I book snowbird car shipping?
faqs.a: Two to four weeks ahead for pickups between mid-December and the end of January, and again for April northbound. In October, November, and May, one to two weeks is usually enough. Booking early locks the price and posts your car before drivers build their peak runs.

faqs.q: Should the car ship before or after I fly to Florida?
faqs.a: Most snowbirds schedule pickup the day before the flight, fly down, and take delivery two to three days later, using a short rental in between. Having the car waiting when you land means it leaves New York four or five days before you do. Either works; give us the flight date and we plan around it.

faqs.q: Can the truck deliver inside my gated community in Florida?
faqs.a: Often not. Many communities bar large commercial trucks, so the driver meets you at the gatehouse, clubhouse lot, or a nearby shopping center. Ask the community office whether haulers are allowed, get the gate code or guest-list procedure, and tell us any HOA delivery hours so the driver arrives prepared.

faqs.q: Is the Amtrak Auto Train cheaper than shipping the car?
faqs.a: Usually about the same once you count the drive to Lorton, Virginia, the sleeper fare, and the drive from Sanford to your destination. The Auto Train suits people who want to ride with the car and bring extra luggage. Shipping suits people who prefer a short flight or are headed well south of Sanford.
